title: Sector entry frameworks — fine-grained go-to-market angles across five verticals
body:
Purpose
This note synthesizes tactical entry frameworks and differentiated messaging for five priority verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, and gov/defense. Aim is to produce short, testable angle variations (for ads, sales decks, and SDR outreach) plus competitor-framing snippets and rapid objection responses.

Audience
- Growth and demand gen
- Field sellers and solution engineering
- Product marketing for feature prioritization

Executive summary (1 paragraph)
Across these sectors the buying friction clusters around three axes: risk/compliance, predictable economics, and operational reliability at scale. Redwood’s unique levers (dedicated capacity, private deployments, and runtime-level cost controls) let us craft messaging that speaks to each axis explicitly. Below are compact, non-overlapping angle sets per vertical with suggested one-liners, proof points, and competitor reframes to A/B in field experiments.

Format per vertical
- Problem snapshot (1–2 lines)
- Top buyer jobs / personas
- 3 targeted messaging angles (headline + 1 supporting bullet each)
- How to frame competitor pushbacks (concise rebuttal)
- Quick proof signals / POA for sales enablement

1) Fintech — payments, lending platforms, and neobanks
Problem snapshot: Latency spikes and unexpected token costs create margin leakage on high-volume prompts (KYC, risk scoring, transaction enrichment). Compliance teams want data isolation and deterministic audit trails.
Top buyer jobs / personas: Head of Platform, Payments CTO, ML Engineering lead (fraud/KYC), Security & Compliance manager.
Angles:
  A. Predictable inference economics for per-transaction margins
    - Headline: "Turn per-transaction AI costs from a variable to a line item."
    - Support: Reserved pools + batching recommendations lower cost variance by 30–60% on typical scoring workloads.
  B. Compliance-first isolation without slow rollouts
    - Headline: "VPC/private deployments with audit-ready telemetry."
    - Support: Private control plane + KMS integration and token-level logs for forensic reviews.
  C. Risk-tolerant fallbacks for high-throughput pipelines
    - Headline: "Graceful degradation — stay live when models falter."
    - Support: Smart routing to cheaper model variants and automatic fallbacks for capacity loss.
Competitor reframes and rebuttals:
  - "We can just use cloud provider endpoints" → Cloud endpoints lack fine-grained deterministic cost controls and auditability at scale. Redwood maps to business KPIs (cost per approval, latency SLOs) not just tokens.
  - "Open-source stacks are cheaper" → Self-hosting transfers ops risk and adds latency unpredictability; Redwood Dedicated gives cost predictability with SRE-backed SLAs.
Quick proof signals / POA:
  - Benchmark: Show a live before/after cost per approval for a 100k/mo transactions workload.
  - One-pager: Compliance checklist mapping to SOC2/ISO items (for AE use).

2) Healthcare — EHR augmentation, triage assistants, research summarization
Problem snapshot: PHI handling, deployment isolation, and explainability are first-order constraints; clinical teams demand conservative failure modes.
Top buyer jobs / personas: Chief Medical Informatics Officer, Head of Clinical Data, Security/Privacy lead, Product manager (Clinical apps).
Angles:
  A. Auditable PHI controls with customer-managed keys
    - Headline: "PHI never leaves your network unless you allow it."
    - Support: On-prem/private deployment options + HSM/KMS integrations and immutable access logs.
  B. Clinician-first reliability and conservative outputs
    - Headline: "Model outputs designed to err on the side of caution."
    - Support: Tunable response strictness, deterministic fallback to curated rule sets.
  C. Longitudinal data efficiency for medical NLP
    - Headline: "Reduce model costs by caching longitudinal context and KV reuse."
    - Support: Prefix/KV caching reduces tokens for follow-up queries by up to 70% in pilot studies.
Competitor reframes and rebuttals:
  - "Use hosted SaaS—it’s faster to integrate" → Speed is necessary, but not at the cost of PHI exposure. Redwood Private offers near-self-serve speed with enterprise controls.
Quick proof signals / POA:
  - Customer brief: pilot outcome showing latency/SLA and PHI controls for an EHR summarization flow.
  - Tech note for SEs: architecture diagram mapping EHR pipeline -> Redwood Private -> audit logs.

3) Legal — contract review, e-discovery, compliance automation
Problem snapshot: Firms and legal ops want repeatable, defensible outputs and chain-of-custody for generated artifacts; cost is secondary to defensibility and traceability.
Top buyer jobs / personas: GC/Head of Legal Ops, Director of eDiscovery, Product Counsel.
Angles:
  A. Forensic-grade provenance for generated content
    - Headline: "Trace every generated token back to a model, version, and prompt."
    - Support: Versioned model IDs, prompt snapshot logs, and signed attestations for evidentiary trails.
  B. Workflow-native throughput for batch review jobs
    - Headline: "Scale doc review with predictable batch windows and cost controls."
    - Support: Dedicated capacity scheduled for night windows + autoscaling policies tuned for throughput.
  C. Configurable conservatism to reduce hallucination surface
    - Headline: "Constrain model creativity when accuracy matters."
    - Support: Output filters, grounding integrations, and reranking policies to bias for precision.
Competitor reframes and rebuttals:
  - "LLM APIs are faster for proof-of-concepts" → True, but without provenance and version controls you cannot use outputs for defensible legal workflows; Redwood provides both speed and traceability.
Quick proof signals / POA:
  - Legal-safe checklist and demo script for SEs to walk GCs through evidence-chain features.
  - Case study (anonymized) showing reduced review hours and improved audit readiness.

4) Enterprise SaaS — product augmentation and embedded copilots
Problem snapshot: Product teams want low-latency embeddings and chat features with predictable costs and the ability to roll out feature gates across customer tiers.
Top buyer jobs / personas: Head of Product, Platform PM, Engineering Manager, CTO.
Angles:
  A. Feature-grade SLAs and rollout controls
    - Headline: "Ship copilots with release controls, canarying, and predictable latency."
    - Support: Built-in rollout policies, per-route metrics, and model pinning for deterministic behavior.
  B. Cost-aware embeddings and large-scale search
    - Headline: "Keep vector search economically sane at 10M+ queries/month."
    - Support: Quantization and batching recommendations tuned for embedding workloads.
  C. Product-focused developer ergonomics
    - Headline: "Same API for hosted, dedicated, or private — one integration, many deployment modes."
    - Support: SDKs, sample apps, and trace hooks directly consumable by product analytics.
Competitor reframes and rebuttals:
  - "We can just use hyperscaler’s managed model endpoints" → Hyperscalers can be opaque on per-token economics and lack the nuanced rollout controls product teams need. Redwood maps runtime knobs to product KPIs.
Quick proof signals / POA:
  - Sandbox template: feature toggle + canary config that integrates with client analytics SDK.
  - Bench: embedding latency and P99 under a 5M query/day workload.

5) Gov / Defense — classified workflows, audited deployments
Problem snapshot: Air-gapped or regionally isolated deployments, rigorous accreditation, and long procurement cycles. Proof-of-security and predictable custodian controls are higher priority than time-to-launch.
Top buyer jobs / personas: Agency CISO, Program Manager, Systems Integrator, Procurement lead.
Angles:
  A. Accreditation-ready architecture for classified data
    - Headline: "Design patterns for accredited, air-gapped model serving."
    - Support: Private control plane options, on-prem deployable runtime, and supply-chain attestations.
  B. Contract-aware SLAs and operational rigor
    - Headline: "Field-proven SLAs and runbooks for mission continuity."
    - Support: Dedicated capacity with playbooks, SPOF analysis, and integrated tracing for ATO packages.
  C. Interoperability with existing SI stacks
    - Headline: "Integrates with existing SI toolchains and SIAM models."
    - Support: Clear integration points, Terraform modules, and formal change-control patterns.
Competitor reframes and rebuttals:
  - "Big defense contractors already provide hosting" → Integrators provide hosting but not necessarily the inference economics controls nor the modern runtime optimizations Redwood delivers; position Redwood as a modular inference engine partner for SIs.
Quick proof signals / POA:
  - Security pack: package of artifacts (runbooks, KMS diagrams, SOC-like checklist) to accelerate ATO conversations.
  - Reference architecture for air-gapped pilot.

Cross-vertical common playbook (applies to AE and content teams)
- Lead with the buyer job: cost predictability for finance/ops, auditability for security/compliance, and deterministic latency for platform/product.
- Use short A/Bable lines: pick one headline per channel and measure click-to-demo and AE conversion.
- Close with an operational artifact: each pursuit should include a 1-page technical appendix (architecture + controls) and a 3-bullet commercial ask (pilot size, success metrics, timeline).

Competitor landscape notes (short)
- Cloud provider managed endpoints: win on convenience; lose on economic determinism and fine-grained auditability.
- LLM API pure-play vendors: win on UX and model breadth; lose on enterprise deployment modes and private installation.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes: win on control; lose on SRE burden and predictable economics.
Redwood positioning gap: marry runtime economics controls with enterprise deployment choices and production-grade operational tooling.

Open questions / experimental hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: Fintech prospects respond 3x better when we replace a technical headline with a margin-impact headline referencing $/transaction. Test in two vertical-targeted campaigns.
- Hypothesis B: Healthcare trials convert faster when initial pitch emphasizes "PHI never leaves your network" vs. compliance checklist. Run A/B with AE scripts.
- Hypothesis C: Gov/defense opportunities require a technical appendix up front; include it in first outreach and measure meetings booked.

Next steps (week-by-week)
- Week 0–1: Create 5 one-page technical appendices (one per vertical) — SE task force.
- Week 1–2: Generate 6 headlines per vertical and push into demand-gen for small experiments (ads + LinkedIn).
- Week 2–4: Prepare AE playbook: rebuttal bullets, pricing delta narratives, and a standard pilot success metric template.
- Owner for rollout: Marina Koh (GTM PM) with support from Priya (content), Evan (SE), Luis (growth).

Notes-to-self / friction log (raw)
- Need clear numbers from infra team: realistic cost-savings with Dedicated/Private for embedding workloads (ask infra/bench team for 3 sample workloads).
- Get compliance artifact pack from security: KMS/HSM integration docs, data residency, and sample audit logs.
- Link to related experiments: see GTM-4123 and marketing-playbooks PR for copy variations.

Appendix: example outreach snippets (short)
- Fintech SDR cold line: "Hi <name>, teams we work with cut AI cost variability on scoring pipelines by ~40% while keeping latency below 60ms — curious if you'd benchmark a pilot?"
- Healthcare AE opening: "We run EHR summarization inside your VPC and bring audit logs to your security team — could we show a short technical appendix?"
- Legal AE line: "We can show how to sign and trace every generated output — useful for defensible review workflows?"

End of draft.
